newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KLINSMANN ANSWERS BOSNICH'S JIBE WITH TWO GOALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLINSMANN ANSWERS BOSNICH'S JIBE WITH TWO GOALS.

text.p: While Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich was making Nazi-style jibes at Juergen Klinsmann's expense, the German international skipper scored twice as Bayern Munich beat Cologne 4-2 to go second in the Bundesliga at the weekend.
A round-up of this weekend's major soccer league action in Europe:
England
World record signing Alan Shearer scored the only goal to give Newcastle a 1-0 win at Derby and top spot in the table.
Previous leaders Liverpool were beaten for the first time this season and slipped to third after losing 1-0 at champions Manchester United.

Aston Villa's Australian goalkeeper Mark Bosnich made front and back page headlines for giving a Nazi salute to Tottenham fans, baiting him for an incident involving their former hero Juergen Klinsmann two seasons ago when he was knocked unconscious in a challenge by Bosnich.

The Villa goalkeeper was booked for ungentlemanly conduct and interviewed by police after the match which Tottenham won 1-0. Although he apologised on radio afterwards he could still face charges from the police and the football authorities.
Germany

Oblivious to Bosnich's performance in London, Klinsmann, who has had a poor spell recently, silenced his critics with two goals as Bayern won 4-2 at Cologne on Saturday to draw level with VfB Stuttgart at the top of the table.

Klinsmann headed Bayern's opening goal in the 35th minute and then hit a crucial third goal midway through the second half. The victory put Bayern on 23 points, level with leaders Stuttgart who could only draw 2-2 at lowly Hansa Rostock.
Italy

Inter-Milan, down to 10 men after England midfielder Paul Ince was sent off, beat Piacenza 2-0 to go top while champions Milan slumped to a rare 3-0 defeat at Roma and previous leaders Juventus, who also had a man sent off, lost 2-1 at Vicenza.
Ince was sent off in the 37th minute after he apparantly felled Piacenza's Gianpietro Piovani waiting for a corner to be taken. Piovani was himself sent off later for elbowing an opponent.
Netherlands
Leaders Feyenoord were held to a 1-1 draw by lowly Waalwijk but re-opened their two point lead over nearest challengers PSV Eindhoven who drew 1-1 at Fortuna Sittard.
In some ways that was a creditable result as PSV played the last hour with 10 men after goalkeeper Ronald Waterreus was sent off for handling the ball outside the box.
Champions Ajax squandered a chance to close the gap on the leaders when they drew 1-1 at Utrecht.
Scotland
Champions Rangers run of seven successive league wins from the start of the season ended when they lost 2-1 at managerless Hibernian despite taking an early lead through Joerg Albertz.
Rangers had a chance to equalise five minutes from time but Dane Brian Laudrup failed to score with a twice-taken penalty.
Dutchman Pierre Van Hooijdonk scored in the last minute to give Celtic a 1-0 win over Mothwerwell and move them two points behind Rangers.
Spain

Brazilian striker Ronaldo scored two superb goals as Barcelona beat Compostela 5-1 on Saturday to go top. Ronaldo also hit the post and generally gave such an outstanding performance he was even applauded off the field by the sporting home fans.
"Ronaldo could be the latest Di Stefano or Pele," said Compostela manager Fernando Vazquez afterwards.
France
Angry Bastia fans hurled missiles on to the pitch after an unpunished tackle by Monaco's Emmanuel Petit left Slovakian striker Lubomir Moravcik with a fractured ankle in a 0-0 draw.

The referee was also hit by a missile but play was resumed after a short delay. Leaders Paris Saint-Germain moved seven points clear with Brazilian midfielder Leonardo scoring his seventh goal of the season in their 1-0 home win over Lens.
